Five mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 caught (scaling the wrong group, dropping 'wrist' from the arm group, capping the factor at 2), 2 survived, both in experiments/run.py, which produces every headline number: inverting the fastest-step key in best() (run.py:39, the table would report the slowest step) and widening the worst-joint tally filter to ratio > 0 (run.py:71). No test pins any results.txt cell; the tests cover the patching mechanism, not the analysis.
evidence.craft: Read model.py (61 lines), run.py (80), figure.py (21), tests/test_model.py (54), pyproject.toml, and buildbot_carryphase/model.py score() (305). Small and readable; reusing carryphase's scorer unchanged is the right design and the context manager restores the global. Defects: the mechanism is a monkeypatch of a module-level function (P.torque_limits) captured as _BASE at import, so any other patcher or a thread breaks it silently; a limits argument to C.score would be cleaner. run.py:67 labels a set 'fail only on torque' that its filter (run.py:70-71) does not restrict to torque-only failures. results.json stores only the worst joint, so 'the next joints bind' cannot be read from it. figure.py colours bars by equality with the stock value only. A reviewer would accept with those notes.
evidence.claims: Backed and reproduced: every speed and payload in README:8-11 and the project.json summary (4->6 kg with waist x2, 0.10->0.20 m/s at 4 kg, 8 kg at all x2, 10 kg at 0.17 m/s at all x4, H1 18/23 kg at 0.07 only with all, nothing at 30 kg), '12 tests', '990 cases', 'deterministic' (byte-identical rerun). Overstated or wrong: (a) README:8 'The G1's wall is one joint: the waist pitch' is stated generally but holds for one fixed hand pose (0.3 m ahead, 0.6 m up); the sibling project buildbot-holdheat (README:9, pose search, 2026-10-23, before this project) found that at hands 0.15 m ahead and 0.7 m high the stud-carry peak ratio falls from 0.91 to 0.33 and the binding joint becomes wrist pitch, not the waist; not cited. (b) results.txt:23 / README:36 'cases that fail only on torque': 4 of 7 counted G1 4 kg cases and 5 of 9 at 6 kg also put the centre of pressure outside the sole. (c) README:10 H1 'binding joints ... hip pitch (14 to 18 kg) and the elbow (23 kg and up)' rests on 1-3 of 9 cases per payload; at 18-30 kg 6 of 9 H1 cases fail IK, which no torque scaling can rescue, and 30 kg fails on CoP. (d) README:22 limits table omits G1 waist yaw 88, G1 wrist pitch/yaw 5 and H1 torso 200 N.m, all of which are scaled in the 'waist'/'arms' groups. Disclaimer present (README:15).
evidence.fitness: A robotics researcher could reuse the group-scaling wrapper in an afternoon, but the result is a sensitivity of a static/quasi-static torque budget at one posture, which an actuator engineer does in a spreadsheet; nothing is checked against hardware or a vendor peak/continuous table. Nearest prior work, none cited: actuator and morphology co-design (Ha, Coros et al. 2018, 'Computational co-optimization of design parameters and motion trajectories for robotic systems', IJRR; Fadini et al. 2021, energy-efficient legged-robot actuator sizing; Chadwick et al. 2020, Vitruvio leg design), Unitree's own published joint torque specifications, and in this repository buildbot-holdheat (continuous rating and pose search) and buildbot-payload. Not new as a method; the 'waist pitch is the G1's limit at a forward-reach carry pose' finding is plausible and reproducible but already in buildbot-holdheat's headline (0.54 of peak empty-handed). Standalone (project.json programme 'none').
evidence.domain: Departs from actuator-sizing practice in three places a senior engineer would hit first: (1) the limit used is the Menagerie actuatorfrcrange, a peak torque; a sustained carry is sized against the continuous (thermal) rating, typically a third to a half of peak, and the sibling buildbot-holdheat shows nothing is sustainable at this pose for a continuous rating <= 0.5 of peak; the Limitations section (README:38-43) does not mention it. (2) Posture is held fixed; a practitioner first re-poses the load (hands in, torso upright) before upgrading a motor, and holdheat's pose search shows that moves the bottleneck off the waist. (3) Scaling the limit with mass and inertia fixed is disclosed (README:40). The single-support LIPM gait, CoP and friction checks are standard (Kajita 2001) and correctly applied by the reused scorer; the step grid is coarse but disclosed.

defects.what: Headline 'The G1's wall is one joint: the waist pitch' is a single-pose result stated generally; the in-repo buildbot-holdheat pose search (earlier) moves the binding joint to wrist pitch at a closer-in hold, and is not cited, so 'upgrade the waist' (Next steps) is not the supported action

Limits are Menagerie peak torques (actuatorfrcrange); a sustained carry is sized against the continuous rating, which buildbot-holdheat shows makes nothing sustainable at this pose for rho <= 0.5; not in Limitations
experiments/run.py, which computes every headline number (best() and the worst-joint tally), is untested: inverting the fastest-step key and widening the tally filter both leave all 12 tests green
results.txt/README label the worst-joint tally 'cases that fail only on torque' but the filter (ik ok and ratio > 1) admits CoP failures: 4 of 7 G1 4 kg cases also have the CoP outside the sole
H1 'binding joints are hip pitch then elbow' rests on 1-3 of 9 cases; 6 of 9 H1 cases at 18-30 kg fail IK and 30 kg fails CoP, which torque scaling cannot fix, and the README does not say so
Limits table omits limits that the groups scale: G1 waist_yaw 88, G1 wrist pitch/yaw 5, H1 torso 200 N.m
No prior work cited (actuator/morphology co-design, Unitree joint specs, buildbot-holdheat); the finding duplicates holdheat's waist-pitch headline
Mechanism monkeypatches the module global P.torque_limits (captured as _BASE at import); any concurrent patch or thread silently breaks it; a limits parameter to C.score would be explicit

verdict: The numbers are right and reproducible: a full rerun under MuJoCo 3.3.7 is byte-identical, an independent statics calculation reproduces the waist-pitch torque within 1.7%, and the speed table and the physics invariants (limits never touch the dynamics) check exactly. It does not meet the bar: verification is 2 (run.py, which produces every headline number, is untested; 2 of 5 mutants survived) and claims are 2 (the 'one-joint wall' is a single-pose, peak-torque result stated generally, contradicted for posture by the repo's own buildbot-holdheat; the 'torque-only' tally includes CoP failures; the H1 story is mostly IK and CoP). As research it is a sensitivity run on a static torque budget with no prior work cited, a useful note inside a programme rather than a result a humanoid actuator engineer would act on.
